
Forge did not edit any existing file. Wire the resource by hand:

  1. Declare the new modules (each in the listed file, keeping `mod` lines sorted):

       src/domain/entities/mod.rs             pub mod event;
       src/application/ports/mod.rs           pub mod event_repository;
       src/application/use_cases/mod.rs       pub mod events;
       src/infrastructure/database/mod.rs     pub mod events;
       src/adapters/http/mod.rs               pub mod access;
       src/adapters/http/mod.rs               pub mod streams;
       src/adapters/http/mod.rs               pub mod events;
       src/adapters/http/views/mod.rs         pub mod events;

  2. In src/bootstrap/mod.rs, at the end of `fn compose`, before `Ok(())`:

    // events: tenant-scoped, under /tenants/{tenant_id}/events. RBAC denies
    // every role `policy` does not name: the `owner` role (`setup` gives it to
    // the first member) may read and write; grant other tenant roles here.
    let mut policy = forge::security::RbacPolicy::new();
    let owner = forge::security::Role::new("owner").map_err(forge::ComposeError::other)?;
    for permission in [
        crate::application::use_cases::events::READ_PERMISSION,
        crate::application::use_cases::events::WRITE_PERMISSION,
    ] {
        let permission =
            forge::security::Permission::new(permission).map_err(forge::ComposeError::other)?;
        policy.allow(owner.clone(), permission);
    }
    let pool = composition.postgres()?.pool().clone();
    // Sessions end after FORGE_AUTH_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT without a request.
    let sessions = crate::infrastructure::auth::PostgresSessionStore::new(pool.clone())
        .with_idle_timeout(
            forge::auth::SessionIdleTimeout::new(composition.config().auth.session_idle_timeout)
                .map_err(forge::ComposeError::other)?,
        );
    let access = crate::adapters::http::access::SessionTenantAccess::new(
        std::sync::Arc::new(sessions),
        std::sync::Arc::new(crate::infrastructure::tenancy::PgMembershipStore::new(pool)),
        policy,
    );
    // Live updates (--broadcast), once for every broadcasting resource. On
    // PostgreSQL every replica hears every change (LISTEN/NOTIFY); production
    // needs FORGE_STREAMS_KEY (`openssl rand -base64 32`, the same everywhere).
    let streams =
        crate::adapters::http::streams::Streams::register(composition, forge::Fanout::Postgres)?;
    let events = crate::application::use_cases::events::EventService::new(std::sync::Arc::new(
        crate::infrastructure::database::events::PgEventRepository::new(
            composition.postgres()?.clone(),
        ),
    ));
    crate::adapters::http::events::routes(
        composition.router(),
        &site,
        events,
        std::sync::Arc::new(access),
        &streams,
    )?;

  Every route asks the access policy for `events:read` or `events:write`
  first; src/adapters/http/access.rs explains the deny-by-default choice.
  Live updates: create, update and delete publish to the `events` channel of the tenant, and
  the index page subscribes; a stream is served only to callers the same policy
  grants `events:read` (src/adapters/http/streams.rs).
  Permissions match exactly: index and show need `events:read`, new, create,
  edit, update and delete need `events:write`. Signed-out browsers are sent
  to /session/new (the sign-in pages of `forge new` or
  `forge generate authentication`). To allow a read-only tenant role, add after
  `let mut policy`, for example:

    let viewer = forge::security::Role::new("viewer").map_err(forge::ComposeError::other)?;
    let read =
        forge::security::Permission::new(crate::application::use_cases::events::READ_PERMISSION)
            .map_err(forge::ComposeError::other)?;
    policy.allow(viewer, read);

  Then apply the migration (`cargo run -- migrate` with FORGE_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL)
  and run `cargo test` (repository tests on a database server need
  `cargo test -- --include-ignored` and FORGE_TEST_* URLs, see docs/database.md).

Forge did not edit any existing file. Wire the resource by hand:

  1. Declare the new modules (each in the listed file, keeping `mod` lines sorted):

       src/domain/entities/mod.rs             pub mod post;
       src/application/ports/mod.rs           pub mod post_repository;
       src/application/use_cases/mod.rs       pub mod posts;
       src/infrastructure/database/mod.rs     pub mod posts;
       src/adapters/http/mod.rs               pub mod posts;
       src/adapters/http/views/mod.rs         pub mod posts;

  2. In src/bootstrap/mod.rs, at the end of `fn compose`, before `Ok(())`:

    // posts: global. DenyAll refuses every request until you decide who may
    // use them: implement GlobalAccess (src/adapters/http/access.rs).
    let posts = crate::application::use_cases::posts::PostService::new(std::sync::Arc::new(
        crate::infrastructure::database::posts::PgPostRepository::new(
            composition.postgres()?.clone(),
        ),
    ));
    crate::adapters::http::posts::routes(
        composition.router(),
        &site,
        posts,
        std::sync::Arc::new(crate::adapters::http::access::DenyAll),
        &streams,
    )?;

  Every route asks the access policy for `posts:read` or `posts:write`
  first; src/adapters/http/access.rs explains the deny-by-default choice.
  Live updates: create, update and delete publish to the `posts` channel, and
  the index page subscribes; a stream is served only to callers the same policy
  grants `posts:read` (src/adapters/http/streams.rs).

  Then apply the migration (`cargo run -- migrate` with FORGE_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL)
  and run `cargo test` (repository tests on a database server need
  `cargo test -- --include-ignored` and FORGE_TEST_* URLs, see docs/database.md).
